newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy unions to mull action on Italy budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy unions to mull action on Italy budget.

text.p: Italy's three main trades union confederations said on Thursday that their leaderships would meet next Monday to consider protest action over the 1997 budget.

Leaders of the CGIL, CISL and UIL unions announced the plan after talks with Prime Minister Romano Prodi which they said had not provided satisfactory answers to their questions on the package. They did not specifically refer to strike action.

"There has not been a breakdown (of talks) but there is a deep crisis because we put questions and did not receive precise answers, only procedural details," CGIL leader Sergio Cofferati told reporters after the five-hour meeting.
"On Monday we will decide the shape and form of a mobilisation," he said.

Prodi's 1997 budget aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($42 billion) from next year's deficit, the bulk of it from increased revenues including a one-off "Euro-tax" to help Italy make the grade for membership of Europe's planned single currency.
Union leaders said their worries concerned not only the "Euro-tax" but also planned reform to the fiscal system and property tax as well as job creation and wage settlements.
